data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Biological fitness is reproductive success; scientific fitness is resistance to falsification.","Organisms do not consciously conjecture; scientists do.","Nature has no 'truth' goal, whereas science arguably does (even if unattainable)."],"overturn_conditions":["If scientific progress requires a positive measure of truth-likeness (verisimilitude) which corroboration cannot provide.","If acting on a theory logically entails assigning it higher subjective probability."],"shared_structure":["Selection occurs via elimination of unfit candidates rather than confirmation of fit ones.","Survival indicates past fitness in a specific environment, not future guarantee.","Preference for the survivor is pragmatic (it works now) not probabilistic (it is likely eternal)."],"source_memory_refs":["biological_natural_selection","survival_of_the_fittest_organism"],"transfer_claims":["Just as we bet on the surviving species to continue thriving until proven otherwise, we bet on the corroborated theory.","Survival proves nothing about the intrinsic 'truth' of the organism/theory, only its compatibility with current constraints."]},"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms not as an inductive inference of truth, but as a critical selection mechanism analogous to natural selection: we prefer the theory that has survived the severest tests because it is the one currently best fitted to solve problems, even though this survival grants it no higher probability of being true. The cost of accepting this defense is the abandonment of 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) as a measurable guide for theory choice, leaving science with a procedural rule for action that lacks a guaranteed trajectory toward truth.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the Miller-Tich\u00fd refutation of verisimilitude holds universally, then Popper cannot claim the surviving theory is closer to the truth, only that it is less falsified so far.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'acting on the best theory' implicitly requires believing it is more likely to succeed in future untested cases, then the preference smuggles in induction despite Popper's denials.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distinction between 'logical justification' and 'pragmatic necessity' collapses under the weight of scientific decision-making, then the defense fails to address the normative core of the problem.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Evolutionary Epistemology via Severe Testing: The mechanism treats theories as conjectures and severe tests as environmental selectors. Preference is assigned to the survivor not because the survivor is 'more likely true' (induction), but because the elimination of rivals leaves it as the only viable instrument for current problem-solving. This shifts the justification from 'probability of truth' to 'fitness for purpose' relative to known errors.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
